To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the RAS mutation in combination with EGFR and HER-2/neu upregulation is associated with poor outcome in cholangiocarcinal carcinoma.

(1) EGFR and HER-2/neu upregulation is associated with a poor prognosis in CCA, and (2) the KRAS mutation confers resistance to EGFR targeted therapies in CCA cells, whereas the EGFR and HER 2/neu upregulated CCA cells may benefit from dual tyrosine kinase inhibitor therapy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the role of the tumor microenvironment in cancer progression and metastasis.
the development of a new method of measuring the performance of a single-layered system.
the development of novel, highly selective, potent and orally active tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI), which are currently in clinical trials.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the EGFR and HER 2/neu overexpression and KRAS mutation status in peripheral and hilar CCA patients may represent potential predictive markers for the use of tyrosine kinases inhibitors.

the subgroup of CCA paents bearing EGFR and/or HER2/neu overexpression nd KRAS wild-type may benefit from a dual-target tyrosine kinase inhibitor therapy, but only if the clinical/pathoogic parameters known to date as prognostic factors are available.

the subgroup of patients with EGFR, HER2/ neu up-regulation, and KRAS wildtype should be included in future clinical trials of tyrosine inhibitors in order to verify the efficacy of these drugs in the subgroup of patients harboring these specific genomic alterations.
